# Handoff to Antigravity: AI illustrations for rowbose.com/future

Branch: `claude/gifted-babbage-45gl24` (commit `a338228` and later). Read `AGENTS.md` first; this file only adds what is specific to this task.

## Where things stand

The page `site/future/index.md`, the whitepaper `site/future/whitepaper.md` and its PDF are done. The four figures are
**drawn SVG** (`site/assets/future/*.svg`, generated by `scripts/future/figures.mjs`). They are accurate to the paper
but they are diagrams, not AI illustrations. `AGENTS.md` ("Documentation Diagrams & Visuals") asks for AI-generated
images alongside the Mermaid text, and the `robos:FlowDiagram` shape describes `robos:imagePath` as an AI-rendered image.
No image model was available in the session that built this, so that part is missing.

## The task

Generate one AI illustration for each figure, using your image model:

| Figure | Source of truth | What it must show |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `commons-map` | `site/assets/future/commons-map.svg` | People, AI agents and companies add skills through one gate. A job is broken into smaller jobs, then base tasks (bricks) that many apps reuse. A small AI on a laptop, plus a private company shelf, snaps bricks into a finished app. |
| `assembler-loop` | `assembler-loop.svg` | Five steps: describe, break down, look up, machines check the fit, pieces run their own tests. A missing piece is built once and the lookup runs again. |
| `worked-example` | `worked-example.svg` | One request becomes four smaller jobs and seven bricks: five reused, one from the clinic's private shelf, one missing and built once. |
| `skill-lifecycle` | `skill-lifecycle.svg` | Propose, find a twin, check, build reproducibly, sign and log, share to mirrors. Duplicates link to the existing skill; failing tests go back. |

Style rules come from `AGENTS.md`: professional, clean, developer-friendly, crisp schematic, legible labels, **no
decorative bling**. Palette to match the site: cyan `#22d3ee` for the commons, violet `#a78bfa` for private company
material, amber `#fbbf24` for "new, built once", green `#34d399` for "already exists, reused", on navy `#0b1220`.

Image models garble text. Either generate with no embedded text and overlay labels, or check every word against the
SVG. Do not let an image add a claim the paper does not make (no numbers, no logos, no "100% secure").

## Where it goes

1. Save as `site/assets/future/ai/<figure>.jpg` (about 1600 px wide).
2. Use them as illustration on `site/future/index.md`; **keep the SVG diagrams** as the accurate figures, and keep the
   whitepaper figures as SVG so the PDF stays reproducible. Propose a different placement if you see a better one.
3. Point each node's `robos:imagePath` at the new image (nodes `urn:robos:diagram:skill-commons-<figure>` in the
   `documentation` KGraph package) and leave their `robos:mermaidText` as is.
4. Conventional commit on this branch, push to `origin claude/gifted-babbage-45gl24`. No PR unless asked.

## Traps (these cost time last time)

* **Do not use the default `kgraph` CLI to edit the repo graph.** It writes to `~/.robos`, not `./.robos`. Build the store
  the way the repo's tests do: `new SDLCKnowledgeGraphStore({ filePath: '.robos/knowledge-graph.jsonld', rootDir: '.robos' })`.
  Saving re-syncs the aggregate file and drags in unrelated tabletop nodes that were already stale in `HEAD`. Commit only
  your own node changes. Its `robos:nodes` and `@graph` lists must stay identical, and the file has no trailing newline.
* The graph has 12 pre-existing SHACL violations in unrelated nodes. Your change should add none.
* **Do not run the documentation test suites to "check your work".** They regenerate tracked files (`docs/schemas/**`,
  `.robos/elearning.yaml`). If you do, `git checkout` the strays before committing.
* `*.pdf` is git-ignored except `site/future/skill-commons-whitepaper.pdf`.
* Rebuild after changing figures: `scripts/build-future-whitepaper.sh`. To preview the site: see `site/README.md`.

## Out of scope

The whitepaper text. Its citations were checked from search-result summaries only (no direct page access), so a human
should spot-check them, especially the DéjàVu duplication percentages in section 1.1, before relying on them.
